tasks.notes: Commit ff556c785. Declared `.default(false)` WITHOUT `.optional()`, deviating from the three sibling flags (profileCompleted/setPasswordPrompted/serviceSuspended): the column is NOT NULL DEFAULT false, and `.optional()` would only widen the output type to `boolean | undefined` for a case the DB cannot produce, forcing `?? false` on every predicate consumer. It also would NOT deliver the task's 'default is false' requirement — `z.boolean().default(false).optional()` is ZodOptional<ZodDefault<>>, which short-circuits on an absent key and yields `undefined`, never the default. Cost of the stricter type: three object literals had to declare the field (user.http.schema.ts's httpToDomainUserCreate, apps/api's admin create route, and 3 test factories). SCOPE ADDITION the task did not list: `isSystemAccount` must also be OMITTED from UserUpdateInputSchema. Zod 4's `.partial()` keeps `.default()` and BaseCrudService.update re-parses through that schema (SPEC-217 precedent, documented in the file's own JSDoc), so leaving it settable means any unrelated profile save re-injects `false` and clears the flag — turning a staff account back into an indexable author page, i.e. the AC-16/R-9 bug arriving through a different door. Verified absent from every public projection: UserPublicSchema, UserListItemSchema, UserSummarySchema and the route-local UserAuthorPublicResponseSchema are all explicit allow-lists (`.pick()` or hand-written z.object), so the only `.omit()`-based derivations are the create/update inputs. Repo-wide typecheck 41/41, schemas 7201/7201, service-core 7479/7479, api admin-create-restore 16/16, lint 0 errors, type-cast guard green.

tasks.notes: Commit 252585a21 (0034-system-account-flag-staff.ts). NOT contentOnly — T-038's rule applies: this migration's rows exist on a fresh build because T-004's fixture produces them. Predicate is `email IN (2) AND is_system_account = false`, so a second run flags 0 and an operator-flagged row is never rewritten. An environment missing the accounts (a prod bootstrap with --required --exclude=users never creates them) is a silent skip, NOT a throw — a throw aborts the whole batch (HOS-25 G-5) for a legitimate condition. Tested against the real integration DB with rollback isolation rather than a stubbed ctx.db, because this migration IS its WHERE clause and a stub would only assert that a fluent chain was written. 4 tests: two flagged + a staff-role PERSON left alone (the point of a stored flag over a live role check), idempotent second run, absent-accounts no-op, already-flagged row not rewritten. Trap noted in the test: 'superadmin@hospeda.com'.includes('admin@hospeda.com') is TRUE, so a bare toContain(ADMIN_EMAIL) would pass even when the wrong row was flagged — the negative assertion is what pins it. DUAL-WRITE GUARD VERIFIED NON-VACUOUSLY: committed T-004 alone first and confirmed scripts/check-seed-dual-write.sh FAILS naming both fixtures, then this commit made it pass.

tasks.notes: Commit e27d2d0c9 (0035-editorial-author-slug.ts). Both halves of the dual-write in one commit: 0025's ensureEditorialAuthor now passes slug: EDITORIAL_SLUG at creation (so a fresh environment never generates the auto-slug), and 0035 renames already-seeded ones. contentOnly: true per T-001's M-B verdict — the row has no fixture baseline, it exists only because 0025 (itself contentOnly) created it. The created_by_id IS NULL clause is what keeps anything a human actually created untouched — do not drop it. This rewrites 44 live production rows, so log the affected count before and after. tasks.notes: Commit 71295ab59 (0036-reattribute-imported-events.ts). contentOnly: true per T-001's M-C verdict. DEVIATION FROM THE TASK TEXT, deliberate and tested: the EDITORIAL account resolves by email as specified, but the SOURCE account resolves by superadmin@hospeda.com FIRST and falls back to ctx.actor.id when that account is absent. Reason: findSuperAdminActor (runner.ts:158) returns ANY user holding SUPER_ADMIN, and the documented prod bootstrap (`--required --exclude=users`, promote a real person, THEN run the ledger — docs/deployment/first-time-setup.md) never creates superadmin@hospeda.com. On that path 0027/0028 attribute every imported event to the REAL person's account, and an email-only lookup would find nothing, skip silently, and leave 44 imports published under a human being's public author page — the same class of harm the spec exists to prevent, one identity over. The widening is safe because `created_by_id IS NULL`, not the author identity, is what excludes human-authored content. This became reachable only after T-037/T-038: pre-contentOnly, 0027/0028 never ran on a fresh build, which is why T-001's doc calls M-C a fresh-build no-op. Verified in the local DB before writing: 52 events author=superadmin/created_by NULL, and 23 events by admin/carlos/laura all with created_by NOT NULL. No deleted_at clause on purpose — attribution is provenance, not visibility; a restored soft-delete must not republish the super-admin byline. 5 integration tests, including one that pins the fallback does NOT shadow the primary lookup when both accounts exist.

tasks.notes: Verified 2026-08-02; both tracks agree on all six facts. Procedure recorded in docs/fresh-build-parity-verification.md. MIGRATED track: db:push + db:seed:migrate on the worktree DB, which was genuinely pre-HOS-375 (no is_system_account column, editorial on auto-slug user-76eb2960, 52 events on the super admin). FRESH track: a DEDICATED throwaway database (hos375_freshbuild) + db:migrate + db:apply-extras + full seed + --baseline-stamp. CRITICAL DEVIATION FROM THE TASK TEXT: `pnpm db:fresh-dev` was NOT run and MUST NOT be — every worktree DB plus hospeda_dev and hospeda_template live in the SAME container, and its `docker compose down -v` destroys that volume, i.e. every worktree on the machine. Result on both tracks: slug equipo-hospeda, both staff flagged, 0 super-admin orphan events, 52 events + 22 posts on the editorial account. AC-18 over the fresh build's 36 ledger rows: the 5 contentOnly migrations 'ok', the other 31 'baseline-stamp', zero violations. KEY FINDING: which half produces the end state DIFFERS per migration. 0034's flag comes from the FIXTURE (it was stamped and never ran) — correct, which is why it is not contentOnly. 0035 RAN but was a no-op, because 0025 already writes the slug — the correct outcome for a well-formed dual-write. 0036 moved 52 rows on the FRESH build too, because 0027/0028 create the events attributed to the acting actor and no fixture can produce them pre-attributed; had it been stamped, a fresh build would ship 52 events under /autores/super-admin-user/ while a migrated one shipped zero. That is the concrete case justifying the contentOnly flag. Two tooling gotchas documented: db:migrate FAILS on a worktree DB (built with db:push, __drizzle_migrations empty, so it replays from 0000 onto an existing schema — use db:push there), and drizzle-kit swallows its own errors when stdout is not a TTY (exit 1, no message) — diagnose by calling the migrator programmatically and logging error.message.

tasks.notes: Commits 103ad6f17 (flags), 57bee735c (super-admin guard), f422866ac (docs). SCOPE GREW mid-task, with owner approval: T-037's fall-through means `--baseline-stamp` now really runs migrations, and `runMigrations` resolved its actor via `loadSuperAdminAndGetActor()`, which CREATES the seeded superadmin@hospeda.com account (plus credential row) when none exists. On the prod day-1 path — seeded `--required --exclude=users` precisely to keep that predictable credential off the box, with the ledger step documented BEFORE the real admin is created — the fall-through would have silently undone the exclusion. The pre-existing manual workaround had the same hole, but opt-in. The lookup takes the run's Drizzle client explicitly — reading `getDb()` failed in the integration suite with 'Database not initialized' (the documented dist-vs-src double-instance), so threading the client is correctness, not test convenience.
